name: אֲחֻזָּם
summary: A man of Judah, son of Ashhur and Naarah (1Ch 4:5–6), known only from the genealogy. The name looks like the noun אֲחֻזָּה “possession” with the ending -ām, read either as “their possession” or as a noun of the person, “possessor”; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Naarah bore him Ahuzzam (אֲחֻזָּם), Hepher, Temeni and Haahashtari.”

note: Takes a.cl.ae (1 token). Whether -ām is the suffix “their” or a name-forming ending is not settled.
